name: a collapse-state change schedules no filter refresh
why: Removes the _scheduleCollapseStateFilterRefresh() call from _applyExpandedCellState(). The 📊 counts still keep up (the uniq-drop cache is dropped either way), but picking the same Structure entry again replays the row list from before the toggle. Must fail on 'B: the second pick renders one row fewer, not the first pick's row list' (45 expected, 46 rendered).

name: the refresh no longer drops any cached row list
why: Keeps the scheduled re-run but removes _invalidateFilterCacheWhere(), so runFilter() is served the list cached under the entry's own key. Must fail on the same B assertion — the drop, not just the re-run, is load-bearing.

name: the key predicate misses the collapsed mode
why: Narrows _filterKeyReadsCollapseState() to the expanded mode alone. A key built from '▶ collapsed multi-row cells' then survives the drop and is replayed. Must fail on B — the predicate's content matters, not just its existence.

name: an active filter is not re-run after a toggle
why: Keeps the cache drop but never re-runs, so a row expanded while 'collapsed multi-row cells' is filtering stays on screen under a state it no longer has. Must fail on 'D: the expanded row leaves a collapsed-cells filter it no longer matches'.

name: the no-op gate is dropped (state written that was already there)
why: Without `was !== expanded`, every write schedules a refresh even when the state did not change — e.g. the mass-toggle pass re-asserting the state cells already have. That is wasted work, not a wrong answer, so no assertion here can see it. KNOWN UNCOVERED: catching it needs a render or filter-pass counter.

name: the per-frame coalescing guard is dropped
why: Every toggled cell would then schedule its own refresh, so a column-header or global mass toggle re-runs the filter once per cell instead of once. A cost, not a wrong answer. KNOWN UNCOVERED, same reason as the gate above.
